newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina mulls launching five-year peso bond - DyN.
newsitem.headline: Argentina mulls launching five-year peso bond - DyN.

text.p: Argentine Economy Minister Roque Fernandez was quoted by the local news agency DyN Monday as saying the government is considering issuing a five-year peso-denominated bond.

"Everybody is recommending that we do it to give a positive signal of confidence in the local currency to overseas investors," DyN quoted him as saying in London. "They are telling us to do something in pesos, even though it's slightly more expensive."
He said the government is considering an issue of more than $300 million, which would trade some 250 basis points over U.S. Treasuries, a level considered expensive by the government.
Still, Fernandez said this high yield would lead to demand from banks for the bond.
The economy minister added in the interview that at the beginning of 1997, Argentina may sell a "significant amount" through a yen bond issue.
Fernandez added that "we have not discarded" the possibility of swapping old for new debt.
